rv.q: Director Joanna Bowman, a rising star in Scottish theatre, realises all this with assurance, unfolding the action with an astute mix of fluid naturalism and directorial flair.
It’s a testament to Lynn Nottage’s script, which premiered off-Broadway in 2016, that it carries its resonances so powerfully and explores its issues in a way that doesn’t feel strained.
Bowman’s production is punctuated by little bursts of techno music care of composer Patricia Panther.

cn.t: Nottage's Pulitzer-winning drama about American capitalism and fraying community receives superbly realized staging that transcends its rust-belt setting to reveal universal resonance, with critics hailing its mighty, Steinbeck-esque power.
